work.title: Tragische Kantaten für eine oder zwo Singestimmen und das Clavier

history.p: The present two cantatas, the publication of which includes a detailed introduction addressed to Heinrich Wilhelm von Gerstenberg, are the only ones published during Scheibe’s lifetime. In 1761, when he and his family returned to Copenhagen from Sønderborg where he had established a music school for children, the family seems to have moved around for a few years, and one of the places where Scheibe stayed was in Gerstenberg's house. Gerstenberg was renowned for bringing together German intellectuals residing in Copenhagen to discuss various subjects also including music. It was at this time that Scheibe was deeply absorbed in rhetorical and rhythmical studies of music and poetry, discussing the subject with Gerstenberg as well as Friedrich Gottlieb Klopstock – both were part of the German intellectual circle. In 1765 Scheibe published this collection of two cantatas for solo harpsichord and voices. The text to the first one, 'Ariadne auf Naxos', was by Gerstenberg while the second cantata, 'Prokris und Cephalus', is to a text by Scheibe's friend Johann Elias Schlegel. Scheibe had already composed music to the latter text when he received it in 1747 (see introduction to SchW B2:432). Thus the second cantata is a reworking of the earlier one. The publication created a great interest among intellectuals and composers of the day, not least due to Scheibe’s extensive introduction in which he in detail analyses the works in terms of declamation (arias, recitatives) and provides information on performance practice issues. The two cantatas were reviewed in several journals at the time, among others Bibliothek der schönen Wissenschaften (1765) as well as in Allgemeine deutsche Bibliothek (1769) where the reviewer, the composer Johann Friedrich Agricola, writes extensively on problems regarding the instrumentation, the framework, declamation and the function of the recitative. Agricola refers often to Scheibe's theoretical articles that appeared around that time in Bibliothek der schönen Wissenschaften, 1764–65 (SchW C1:003–005), concluding that 'the space forbids us to continue. I cannot help thinking that in these two cantatas either the composer has not quite felt the storm of the passions and the phrases of the poet or just this time has not been inventive enough to express what he felt simple and happy. We always admire the critical efforts of Mr. Kapellmeister Scheibe's musical writings. But his compositions are not as beautiful as his critical works.' In 1779 a reprint appeared with a slightly different title emphasising Gerstenberg and his cantata, 'Ariadne auf Naxos'. The plates and layout are the same suggesting that they were bought by Hellmann from Korte in Flensburg.The new title page suggests that perhaps Gerstenberg wished to promote himself at the expense of Schlegel whose appearance on the new title page is somewhat down-played. Scheibe's three theoretical articles (SchW C1:003–005) include some important remarks on the cantatas, and the composer also suggests some emendations to the recitatives.

annot.p: 'Wir sind von den Oden unvermerkt zu den Arien und Cantaten gezogen worden, und ein paar zu den letztern gehörige Stücke verdienen hier noch beygebracht zu werden. Der Herr Capellmeister Scheibe gab vor einigen Jahren davon zwo, unter dem Titel: tragische Cantaten heraus. Leb und Tadel finden nirgends mehr Widerspruch, als bey den Arbeiten des Herrn Scheibe: wir enthalten uns also, bey aller Hochachtung, die wir von diesem berühmten und verdienten Manne haben, darüber zu urtheilen. Wenn die Schönheiten der Musik relativisch sind, so kann es nicht fehlen, daß Herr Scheibe, und alle Componisten, hier mehr gelobt, hier mehr getadelt werden. So viel ist gewiß: man thut Herr Scheibe Unrecht, wenn man ihn bloß mit den Ohren beurtheilt.'

annot.p: 'Der Raum verbietet uns weiter zu gehen. Wir können uns nicht entbrechen zu glauben, daß bey diesen beyden Cantaten der Hr. Verf. entweder den Sturm der darinn enthaltenen Leidenschaften, und die Wendungen der Dichter, nicht recht gefühlt haben, oder eben damals nicht erfindsam genug gewesen seyn müsse, das was er fühlte, simpel und glücklich auszudrücken. Wir verehren immer die kritischen Bemühungen des Hrn. K. Scheibe, zur Aufnahme der Musik. Aber seine Compositionen sind freylich nicht so schön als seine kritische Werke.'

annot.p: In a letter dated 25 November 1764, Herder mentions Scheibe's second article on the recitative (Fortsetzung der Abhandlung übers Recitativ) 'die über die Musikalische Deklamation gute Gedanken liefert und, wenn wir nicht irren den Herrn Kapellmeister Scheibe verräth'. Herder also mentions that Bibliothek der schönen Wissenschaften contains an examination of 'Tragische Kantaten von Gerstenberg und Schlegel: in Musik gesetzt von Scheibe: wir sind nach diesem Geschenk einer doppelten Muse Begierig. Man höre aus der Gerstenbergschen Kantate, die verlaßne Ariadne: [...] Welche Einbildungskraft! welche Sprache! und Accente zur Musik!'
